blocks.text: Who We Are: Redefining Education Through Technology and Empowerment
Education Empowered by Innovation & Passion for the People

At the The Global School of Skills (GSS) (GSS), we are more than an educational institution—we are a Social Enterprise EdTech Pathway College with a mission to make quality, internationally recognized education accessible, affordable, and transformative for individuals worldwide. With a special focus on the underserved, GSS breaks barriers to education, offering international regulated diplomas and executive education courses at a fraction of the cost of traditional universities.
Our Unique Approach to Education

Technology-Driven Excellence Leveraging cutting-edge technology developed in-house, GSS redefines how education is delivered. This innovative platform fosters seamless collaboration with prestigious international universities in the UK, Europe and USA.

Through these partnerships, we provide globally recognized British Diplomas (Levels 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7) regulated by OFQUAL UK and/or endorsed by OTHM UK—ensuring students benefit from an education that is not only world-class but also highly relevant to global career demands.
The Problem We Solve: Transforming Access to Education

Many underserved communities lack access to high-quality education that unlocks personal and organizational potential. This results in systemic challenges, including poverty, inequality, and stagnation in social and economic development. At GSS, we aim to address these issues by creating pathways for individuals to:

items: Break the cycle of poverty
Become future leaders and change-makers
Promote social equity
Foster organizational and community growth
Drive global impact

OTHM QUALIFICATIONS
ATHE

ATHE is a global awarding organisation regulated by Ofqual and the other UK and international regulators. ATHE offers a wide portfolio of vocationally orientated and internationally recognised qualifications - such as business and management, law, computing and healthcare, with many eligibles for UK funding. ATHE qualifications are approved as progression pathways to relevant Bachelor's and Master's Top-Up degrees by a growing number of UK and international Universities, providing significant tertiary education opportunities for learners.
Local Access Points (LAP)

Our Local Access Points enable us to take our qualifications to you instead of expecting you to travel to us. Local Access Points are built around the concept of blended learning, a structured study option that uses a combination of support elements from the GSS Academic team and its partners. GSS will be responsible for course delivery, and your Local Access Point will be responsible for providing IT infrastructure and administrative support.
National Union of Students (NUS)

The National Union of Students is a voluntary membership organisation that makes a real difference to the lives of students and its member students' unions. NUS promote, defend and extend the rights of students and develop and champion strong students' unions.
The UK Register of Learning Providers (UKRLP)

The UK Register of Learning Providers is a 'one-stop' portal used by government departments, agencies, learners, and employers to share key information about learning providers. The UKRLP allows providers to update their information in one place and share this across agencies such as the Skills Funding Agency, the Higher Education Statistics Agency (HESA), the Higher Education Funding Council for England (HEFCE) and UCAS.
The CPD Group

The CPD Group is the leading CPD accreditation organisation, raising CPD Standards and improving CPD Learning by supporting CPD Providers nationally and internationally. With over 11,000 approved providers across 100+ industries and sectors, and operating in 170+ countries worldwide, they have issued more than 2,740,353 certificates. As the first certified CPD accreditation organisation by The CPD Register, The CPD Group accredits thousands of CPD training courses, events, e-learning programs, conferences, workshops and seminars every year, adding significant value for audiences and providers alike.

What is GSS?
GSS is an acronym for The Global School of Skills (GSS).
The The Global School of Skills (GSS) is a British educational institution dedicated to providing a wide range of Undergraduate and Postgraduate courses at an affordable cost.
All learning activities, materials and content are provided online and in some branches of the School, as classroom block teaching styles using modern delivery models to make learning more engaging.
On completion of an GSS full degree course, it will give you recognised academic credits to then "top up" at one of our affiliate UK Universities, thereby, saving you time and money.
Where is GSS Located?
While we have numerous branches, we have the main Headquarters and the main Administrative Quarters.
Does GSS provide Students UAE Visa?

Yes. GSS processes UAE Visas for students depending on the duration of their study with us. Students also have the opportunity to search for a suitable job during the course of study if on a long term study.
Does GSS provide Job for Students?
No, GSS does not provide jobs for students but can assist with the search as requested.
Will I be writing an Examination?
All GSS programmes are assessed by assignments only, there are no exams.
Will I really get a Bachelor's Degree in 2 years?

Yes, students who successfully complete their GSS/OTHM Level 4 & 5 (Accelerated Study Model in 1 year) will receive a Level 4 & 5 Diploma from GSS/OTHM and then proceed to year two with a preferred GSS affiliate UK University.
After the successful completion of the 2nd year, a Bachelors Degree will be issued by the preferred affiliate UK University.
Will I really get a Master's Degree in 12 - 18 months or less?
Yes, students who successfully complete their GSS/OTHM Level 7 Course will receive a Level 7 Diploma from GSS/OTHM and then proceed to the 3rd Semester with a preferred GSS affiliate UK University.
After the successful completion of the 3rd Semester, a Master's Degree will be issued by the preferred affiliate UK University.
Can I go to the UK for graduation?

Students who have successfully completed their studies will graduate in the UK with the rest of the students at their preferred GSS affiliate UK University. (Subject to a successful UK Visa application)

blocks.text: What is the UK CPD?
The UK CPD is an acronym for the United Kingdom Continuing Professional Development Courses.
Our Professional Certificates and the Special Executive Masters Programme Certificates fall under the UK CPD Courses. The UK CPD is Non-credit bearing and Non-Degree Programmes.

The Certificates awarded for our CPD Programmes cannot be used as Full Degree Certificates or disguised as such as it carries no credit and cannot be used to pursue an academic Course. However, the relevancy of the certificate lies in the knowledge of the bearer to demonstrate ground knowledge of the subject the certificate was issued in, and this certificate counts towards the appropriate Continuous Professional Development (CPD).
Are there any English language requirements?
For students who cannot communicate or write in English, we have resources they can access for study alongside our courses.
Once you are able to successfully complete our Level 4, 5, 7 or International Postgraduate (Level 7) Diplomas, then you would have met the required English language requirement.
Level 4 & 5

At this Level, you will need to be at least 18 years old and must have completed your secondary education with at least Credits (C grades) in 5 Subjects of which one of the subjects must be English to be eligible to enrol on the course.
The GSS affiliate UK Universities require a minimum age of 19 before embarking on the Bachelor's Degree Top-up programme. No work experience is required for this Level.
Level 7
At this Level, you will need to have a Bachelor's Degree or a Higher National Diploma Degree.

If you do not have this, you will need to have at least 5 years of Managerial working experience either for an Organization or your own Company and be able to prove this. We will look at each application individually and may consider some exceptions.
Will there be an interview?
Learners who achieve an GSS delivered Level 4, 5 or 7 qualifications are automatically mapped against a standard UK Higher Education qualification framework.

This is a universally recognised framework of credits. Universities can, therefore, award credits against the GSS Level 4, 5 and 7 qualifications to give exemptions from large parts of their formal programmes.
GSS and OTHM Qualifications have pre-agreed arrangements with certain universities to provide credits against programmes either on-campus or off-campus. This is termed the 'University Top-up'.
How do I choose the best course for me?
Learners should first visit the The Global School of Skills (GSS) Courses page online to view the range of courses on offer to decide on what subjects best suit the learner, he/she should:
- Review the modules within the course, do they interest you? Are they relevant to your chosen career path?
- Consider how the course is taught and assessed, do you have the motivation to study via distance learning? Are you able to work independently? Do you thrive better in a classroom study mode?

It is important that learners understand how they learn best and not try to extend themselves too far or too quickly and choose a path that comfortably progresses from their current level of skills and experience.
How do I apply for a course?
Once you have reviewed your preferred Course, your first step is to pay for the Registration Fees after which the Application Form is made available to you either online or on request.
Once you have filled out the Application Form and submitted the supporting documents, your application should be reviewed and approved within 1 - 3 working days.
Once you have received your Conditional Acceptance, you are then required to pay a Commitment Fee so that you are registered on the GSS Learning Portal once the Session commences.
Alternatively, you can call email [email protected] or [email protected] so that they will guide you through the enrolment process.
CREDIBILITY
Who is OTHM Qualifications, UK?
OTHM Qualification is an Ofqual regulated body that awards qualifications for colleges in Courses in Management, Business, Tourism and Health & Social Care.
Please visit www.othm.org.uk for more information.
Who is Qualifi, UK?

Qualifi UK is a leading 21st-century Awarding Organisation founded to meet the developing education and training needs of learners and employers from the UK and around the globe serving the needs of learners and employers in the UK and worldwide every year.
Please visit www.qualifi.net for more information.
How are Universities linked to the Modules?

Learners who achieve an GSS delivered Level 4, 5 and 7 qualifications are automatically mapped against a standard UK Higher Education qualification framework. This is a universally recognised framework of credits.

Universities can, therefore, award credits against the GSS study to give exemptions from large parts of their formal programmes. GSS and OTHM have pre-agreed arrangements with certain universities to provide credits against programmes either on-campus or off-campus. This is termed 'University Top-up'.
How do I change my personal contact details once I have given them to GSS?

All details can be edited through the student dashboard. Once a student has enrolled they can log in to view their course progress, edit their profile and communicate with the Students Support, Academic Support and Technical Support.
Can I still access my Student Dashboard if I have finished my course?
No, access to the GSS Dashboard is deactivated once you complete your studies with GSS.
I have forgotten my username/password and cannot login to my dashboard, how can I get access?
If learners have lost or forgotten their login details, they can request a new password by sending an email to [email protected] for assistance.
PROGRESSION
Will I be able to gain higher education qualification through GSS?
The GSS programmes are mapped against UK higher education qualifications which are fully transferable to a range of other higher education routes and professional qualifications.

On completion of the GSS delivered level 4, 5 and 7 Programmes students will be awarded enough Credits so that they can top up to either a Bachelors or Master's Degree at any of our affiliate UK Universities an GSS University partner.
What potential job opportunities are there after I finish the course?
Once you successfully complete the final stage with the affiliate UK University, you will have a Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree that will open doors to many career options.
STUDENTS' SUPPORT
What do I do if I am struggling?
STUDYING ONLINE WITH GSS
What modules do I need to achieve a qualification?

You need to complete all the modules detailed in your required course option plus all the associated assessments to complete the GSS delivered course and receive the Level 4, 5 or 7 Diplomas. This will give you the recognised academic credits to top up to either a Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree. You can study all the modules at your own pace.
Do I need a specific computer to study with GSS?
As long as you have internet access any computer or tablet can be used to complete the online modules and courses. You can also study on your phone with our mobile-friendly content.
Can I access my dashboard and study on my mobile and tablet?
Yes, but this will only be accessible with an internet connection. All digital interactivity has been coded for compatibility on touch screens. You can also learn the material by printing it off.
What study materials do I need for the online programme?

The modules themselves are sufficient for passing the associated assessments. The modules contain additional accessible resources that learners may wish to follow through to enhance their learning and these are provided within the text. GSS also has extra learning resources such as the e-library to aid your study.
How long will my study take?
GSS has Courses ranging from 1 week to 18 months. The actual duration it takes you to complete your study depends on you.
Does my previous study and experience count towards an GSS course?

There are no exemptions or credits within the GSS system of study and you have to study all the GSS modules to take advantage of our access route. However, if you think you may be exempt from a certain level then please contact us and we will advise you. We can also help you with your top-up enquiries if you already have the necessary qualifications.
Can I personalise my study?

Students can study the modules in any order and at any pace, to qualify for the University Top-up. It is important to note that all of the modules and assignments required for each level have to be completed in order to earn the Degree for the Level.
Can I go to the UK for graduation?

Students who have successfully completed their studies will graduate in the UK with the rest of the students at their preferred GSS affiliate UK University. (Subject to a successful UK Visa application)
What do I get when all the modules and assessments are completed?

Learners who complete the full programme of modules as detailed and also complete the assignments are awarded OTHM Level 4, 5, 7 and International Postgraduate (Level 7) Certificates with the official academic credits.
These qualifications are recognised by UK higher education authorities and by the university sector. The student can then apply to one of our University partners to complete their degree.
Do all modules have an exam?

All modules have an online assessment. Completion of the requisite number of assessments and written assignments will grant the participant a qualification recognised by a number of world-class universities.
How do assessments work?
Assessments are research and assignment based.
What is an interactive learning module?
The interactive activities in the modules include tests, exercises and assessments that provide a guide to a learner's progress through the module.
How can I pay for my tuition fees?
GSS has Bank accounts that will accept payment directly. You can also pay by credit /debit card via a link on your Invoice or directly online.
Will GSS provide a Letter for a UK student visa?
No, but your preferred GSS affiliate UK University can.
Do I need a visa to complete modules/course through GSS?

No visa is required for the online programmes. If a student chooses to take the university top-up programme on campus in the UK, a student visa will be required. Learners should request this through their preferred GSS affiliate UK University.
Can I study anywhere in the world?
Yes. There are no geographical limitations for GSS online courses.

blocks.text: Course Enrollment
Deposits, Fee and Payments
To be given an Unconditional Acceptance and/or book a place on a course, students must pay either
(1) The full tuition fee; or

(2) A minimum deposit of 25% of the total course fees (unless indicated otherwise on the application form, payment page or invoice in which case the terms of those pages or documents shall prevail). All deposits received are for the sole purpose of reserving a place on the course and are NON-REFUNDABLE except in cases of complete withdrawal from the programme of which the Registration and Programme of Study Terms and Conditions (see above) will apply.
AND
This means that if a student changes their mind after enrolling on a course, the registration fee and (in some cases) part of the deposit payment CAN NOT be refunded.
Payment Deadline

All tuition fees must be paid either in part or in full (depending on the Courses/Programme) by the payment deadline and before the commencement date of the Course. The commencement date of the Course is the published date as provided on the Unconditional Acceptance confirming successful enrolment to the The Global School of Skills (GSS) Course/Programme.
Students who have not paid on time may lose their place on the course and may not be granted access to learning.
Dishonoured Payments

A minimum charge of £50.00 will be made to students for all dishonoured payments. The School reserves the right to report offenders to the relevant professional body and the authorities, including, but not limited to relevant & applicable law enforcement agencies in the relevant country.
Overdue Accounts
The School reserves the right to charge interest on overdue amounts, accruing monthly from the date that such payments become due.
Instalment Payment Plan

The School expects all students to adhere to the terms and conditions of their payment plan, which includes submitting payment on the date it becomes due. A failure to comply with the terms and conditions of your payment plan renders any payment plan ineffective. As a result, the School may bring the payment plan to an end and reserves the right to recover all outstanding fees.
Debt Recovery

Please note that in relation to overdue amounts, the School also reserves the right to pass this matter to our debt recovery company without further notification to you. This means that your data will be passed to our debt recovery company for further action. For the avoidance of doubt, should your data be passed to our debt recovery company in order to recover any overdue amounts, your liability to pay will be increased by additional fees and charges.

From time to time, we may offer discounts and fee waivers as part of time-limited promotions, packages, alumni discounts and early-bird offers. The full details, eligibility criteria and terms and conditions associated with any such offers, including any time limits and your responsibilities in order to benefit from any such offer will appear on our website and shall be deemed to be incorporated into these terms and conditions.
Dismissal for Non-Payment
The School reserves the right to dismiss and expel any student at any time for the non-payment of fees. No fees will be refunded where a student is dismissed under this section.
Reporting

The School is required to inform the appropriate authorities, where a student has been removed from our School. The School also reserves the right to report non-payment and delayed payment to credit-reporting agencies.
Fees subject to change

Fees are published separately for each semester and are payable by all students studying at the time unless they have paid full fees prior to the publication of the new fees. Paying a deposit does NOT prevent any fee increase from being applied.
Fees exclusive of Professional Body Charges

All tuition fees exclude amounts payable to professional bodies (if and where applicable) for student registration, exemptions and examination entries. Any such fees are payable directly by the student, and the School accepts no responsibility for such payment.
VAT
When applicable, all amounts quoted would include VAT. Some courses are provided by exempt bodies and are not subject to VAT. Please contact us for further details.
No Deposit Account
Funds received but not utilized or refunded in accordance with these Terms and Conditions will be forfeited to the School.
Changes subject to approval

The student agrees that he/she cannot change, defer or withdraw from the programme without prior consent from the School. Where a student has failed to comply with this clause, they will not be eligible for a refund.
Promotions subject to change
Promotions and offers may have restricted eligibility requirements and may change from time to time.
Value-Added Services

Availability of the online resources, face to face/classroom and other value-added services cannot be guaranteed outside of reasons beyond the School�s control. This is including technical faults and limitations.

In situations of Classroom only or Online-only courses; access to all online resources (if provided) is done ex-gratia and does not form part of any contract for services for the former and access to face to face classes (if provided) is done ex-gratia and does not form part of any contract for services for the latter.
Course Specification subject to change

The School reserves the right to change the courses, tutors, course specifications, lectures, other materials, published programmes, speakers, dates and locations from the previously published materials on the site or any other timetables as well as the right to alter to cancel or change the content of lectures and/or study materials and the identity of tutors at its own discretion.

The school shall discharge its obligations in respect of a specific course by providing teaching which is materially similar to the course specification advertised, notwithstanding the fact that course dates, times and location, and/or the identity of the lecturer may vary from the previously advertised specification.
Materials subject to change

The School may make changes to the material on the website or to the products and prices described in them at any time without notice, although we will provide notice of substantive changes where applicable.
Transfers

Course transfers are only permissible with the Schools prior written consent. To apply to transfer, Students must complete an application form for course transfer (available on request) and pay an administration fee of £250. No transfers will be permissible in the event of a student owing fees to the School or in the event of Students failure to attend a sufficient number of classes either face to face or online. Students may be required to pay additional fees if new course fees are higher. All transfer requests are at the sole and absolute discretion of the School.
Student Communication by Email

The School sends out important student information (including timetable updates, class changes, etc.) exclusively by email. It is the student's sole responsibility to ensure that the School has correct and up-to-date email addresses in our records and that the student opens, reads and acts promptly upon such email notifications.
Courses Non-residential

All courses are non-residential unless specified otherwise, whether as a guest or a registered user. Please read these terms and conditions before you start to use the website. By using our site, you indicate that you accept these terms and conditions and that you agree to abide by them. If you do not agree to these terms of use, please refrain from using our website.
Limitation of Liability

Students attention is particularly drawn to this clause. Liability of The Global School of Skills (GSS) for losses arising from their negligence (except in the case of liability for death or personal injury), breach of contract or otherwise will be LIMITED TO THE FULL AMOUNTS PAID BY THE RELEVANT STUDENT FOR THE PARTICULAR COURSES AND/OR STUDY MATERIALS.

Except in the case of liability for death and personal injury, the The Global School of Skills (GSS) will have NO LIABILITY FOR INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL LOSS OR DAMAGE HOWSOEVER ARISING. We may revise this acceptable use policy at any time by amending this page. You are expected to check this page from time to time to take notice of any changes we make, as they are legally binding on you. Some of the provisions contained in this acceptable use policy may also be superseded by provisions, promotions or notices published elsewhere on our site.
Governing Law

For the purpose of the Data Protection Act 1998 (the Act), the data controller is GSS. GSS shall process the personal data only in accordance with our privacy policy. In addition, the personal data that we collect from you may be transferred to, and stored at, a destination outside the European Economic Area (EEA) please see our Privacy Policy (/privacy-policy) for further details.
Deferral

Students can only defer their session on a course by up to 1 calendar year and can only defer their place on a course by up to 2 calendar years from the date of course commencement. This is subject to a written application; the payment of the deferral/administrative fee as well as the school’s approval. Under no circumstances will deferral be granted for a total of more than two (2) academic years.
Deferments are allowed for a limited time and are subject to Deferment fees as follows:
3 months – £100 Deferment Fees
6 months – £150 Deferment Fees
9 months – £200 Deferment Fees
1 year – £400 Deferment Fees
Between 1 – 2 years £600
Learners must apply to defer a Programme
Students must make an application for deferral at least 28 days (4 weeks) before taking their deferment.

Even if you defer your Programme, your ongoing payments terms or schedules should be adhered to strictly. Payments outside the payment terms/schedules as given on your Payment Tab on the GSS Online Study Portal or your Invoice would be subject to an Administrative or Deferment Charges and any new Tuition Fee (both for GSS Courses/Programmes and our 3rd party Top-ups Programmes) for that Academic year.

Applications to Defer

Applications for deferment, made less than 4 weeks after initial payment are subject to an administration charge deductible from the initial payment made and/or as stated on your Invoice or payment page.

No refund would be given for cancellations less than 14 days to the Programme and there would be an administrative charge for deferment to another Session. No refund would be given for cancellations once a student logs in to the GSS Online Study Portal when the course enrolled for, has been activated on their Portal

Upon deferring their course, students waive their right to apply for a refund. Where a student has deferred their course, and subsequently fails or attempts to withdraw from the course NO REFUNDS WILL BE PROVIDED save in exceptional circumstances. The school has sole discretion in determining whether a student's circumstances are exceptional.
Flexible Payment

Words and expressions defined in the General Terms and Conditions have the same meaning in these additional Terms and Conditions except to the extent that they are varied by these additional Terms and Conditions.

The Flexible Payment Plan enables students to pay their course fees in instalments spread over a maximum of 12 consecutive months and in any event, ultimately determined by our Credit Control Team and at our sole discretion.

Upon enrolment, students are required to pay a minimum deposit of 25% - 30% of the total Course Fees (unless indicated otherwise on the website, Invoice or your Payment page on the GSS Online Study Portal Dashboard), in which case the terms of the Website, Invoice or your Payment Page on the GSS Online Study Portal Dashboard shall prevail).

If you fail in making any due instalment as specified on our Website, Invoice or your Payment Page on the GSS Online Study Portal Dashboard, you would be automatically deferred and the terms and conditions as specified on our Deferral page (https://msbm.org.uk/learning-with-msbm/deferral) would be applicable in that instance.

Leave of Absence

Students sometimes find themselves facing difficulties that affect their ability to undertake their studies, for example, if they are ill or undergoing serious personal problems. A leave of absence enables a student to take an authorised break from their studies in order to overcome the difficulty, without losing valuable time from their registration period, which will be suspended for the duration.

Students must apply for permission from their department and faculty to take a leave of absence, by sending an email officially to [email protected]. Please be aware that once the email is received by the Academics Department, it will normally take up to 2 weeks for Faculty consideration and processing, but may take longer if additional information/clarification is required. Students can apply for LOA on the following grounds:

items: Medical
Personal
Parental (maternity/paternity)
Professional/Work-related
Financial

blocks.text: Requests for LOA on financial grounds are not normally approved but may be considered if a student's financial situation changes due to unforeseen and exceptional circumstances.
Students should not apply for a leave of absence to cover a period of annual leave.

When applying for a leave of absence, appropriate documentary evidence must be supplied in order for the department and faculty to consider whether to approve the request. For a leave of absence on medical grounds, a medical or doctor's note is required that covers the entire period of leave of absence request. Any application made on medical grounds without an appropriate medical note will not be approved.
Students applying for a leave of absence to cover maternity leave should, wherever possible, provide a copy of their 'MAT' form.

It is essential that students notify their supervisor/department as soon as any difficulties arise that might affect their studies and that applications for leave of absence are made promptly and, wherever possible, not retrospectively. Requests for retrospective leave of absence will not normally be approved if they date back further than 45 days.

Absences that are taken without a formal request for leave of absence being made will be treated as unauthorised absences and may trigger further action. During the period of leave of absence, the student will temporarily leave their programme of study and their registration will be suspended for the duration of the absence. Supervision should not be provided during a leave of absence and the student should not undertake any work that relates to their studies.

Students should be aware that requests for an indefinite leave of absence will not be considered. It is unlikely that a request for more than 12 months at a time will be approved and requests to further extend a lengthy leave of absence will be carefully reviewed and may be rejected. There are a number of reasons why lengthy periods away from your studies are not recommended, e.g. the possibility that the study will lose currency and/or originality and changes to departmental structures and staffing, which may mean that appropriate supervision is no longer available.

In certain specific circumstances, there may be occasions when a student is returning from a leave of absence due to ill health or maternity leave but is not yet able to undertake their study full time. Under such circumstances, a 'phased return' to work may be considered. In practice, a student would need to apply for a leave of absence, which, if granted, would cover only a proportional amount of time lost due to these exceptional circumstances, and not the entire period during which these circumstances are a factor.

Referral

Refer your friends (provided they are not already GSS students) to The Global School of Skills (GSS) ("GSS") and when they make their first payment with GSS in accordance with these Terms & Conditions, and successfully enrol for at least 1 programme with GSS you will qualify to receive a discount off your Programme with GSS or a Commission from us ("The Offer").
To participate in the Offer you must recommend at least 1 friend to take the Programme by submitting your friends' details.

The friends you recommend will receive an email from GSS on behalf of you containing an invitation to enrol for the recommended programme or any other programme with GSS. To enrol, the friend needs to do the following before the registration deadline:

items: Pay the Registration Fee
Submit the filled Application Form with the required supporting documents.
Once the Conditional Offer of Acceptance for the Programme has been sent, the Tuition Fee invoiced must be paid either in full or in the preferred Instalment

blocks.text: You will only qualify for the Offer if your referral enrols as stated above and your discount/commission is payable either in full for the full payment or on a pro-rated basis on the Instalment basis.
Once your friend has successfully enrolled a Student Liaison Personnel will be in contact within 48 working hours to discuss the redemption of the Offer.
Before entering any friends email addresses and inviting them to participate in the Offer you must ensure that you have the permission of each friend you recommend to be contacted by GSS.
You may only claim the Offer once per friend enrolled and for 1 Programme only.
By participating in the Offer you agree to be bound by these terms and conditions, and that the decision of GSS is final and binding in all matters relating to this.
GSS reserves the right to cancel or amend the terms of this Refer a Friend Offer without notice.
Any personal data collected for the purposes of the Offer will be processed in accordance with the provisions of GSS's Privacy Policy.
General Refund Policy
Refund and Cancellation Policy

This Refund and Cancellation Policy applies to payments made to the The Global School of Skills (GSS) ("GSS") and should be read together with the applicable Study Contract, Offer Letter, Invoice, Payment Page and programme-specific terms.
All refund requests must be made in writing and will be considered in accordance with this Policy.
Nothing in this Policy affects any statutory rights which cannot lawfully be excluded or restricted.
Non-Refundable Fees

Except where statutory cancellation or refund rights apply, applications for a Tuition Fee refund made less than thirty (30) days before the commencement date of a Course or Programme will not ordinarily be eligible for a refund.

By this stage, GSS may have reserved a place for the student, commenced administrative or academic preparations, activated services, or incurred costs and commitments in connection with the student's enrolment.

Where a refund is required by law, or where GSS agrees to consider a refund in exceptional circumstances, GSS may deduct any amounts which it is lawfully entitled to retain, including the cost of services already provided, non-recoverable third-party costs and reasonable losses arising from the cancellation.
Students should also read the applicable Study Contract with GSS.
Statutory Cancellation Rights
Students purchasing programmes online or otherwise entering into a distance contract as consumers may have a statutory right to cancel within fourteen (14) days of entering into the contract.

Where a student requests immediate access to a Course, Programme, digital content or other service during this cancellation period, GSS may commence delivery once the necessary consent or request has been received.

Where the student has expressly requested immediate supply of digital content and has provided the acknowledgements required by applicable law, the statutory right to cancel may be lost once supply of that digital content begins.
Where services have commenced at the student's request but a statutory cancellation right remains, any refund will be calculated in accordance with applicable law.
Administrative Charges
Where a contractual or discretionary refund is approved, an administrative charge may apply.
Any applicable administrative charge will be stated on the student's Invoice, Payment Page, Study Contract or other relevant payment information.
Administrative charges may reflect reasonable costs associated with processing the student's enrolment, payment, cancellation or refund.
An administrative charge will not be deducted where applicable law requires a refund to be made without such a deduction.
Method of Refund
Where a refund is approved, GSS will ordinarily process the refund:

items: through the same payment method used for the original payment;
to the same card, bank account or other payment source from which the original payment was received; and
in the same transaction currency, where reasonably practicable.

blocks.text: GSS will not normally make a refund to a different person or unrelated bank account.
Where the original payment method is no longer available, GSS may request additional information before approving an alternative payment method.

Evidence of payment, proof of identity, bank statements or other reasonable documentation may be requested where necessary to verify the payment source or comply with financial, fraud-prevention, anti-money-laundering or other regulatory requirements.
Where currency conversion is involved, GSS is not responsible for any difference resulting from exchange-rate movements or fees imposed by banks, card issuers or payment providers.
Payments and Disbursements to Third Parties
GSS may incur costs or make payments to third parties in connection with a student's application, enrolment or participation in a Programme.
These may include, but are not limited to:

items: awarding or accrediting body registration fees;
university registration or progression fees;
courier charges;
examination or assessment fees;
visa-processing charges;
accommodation;
flights;
event-related charges; and
other third-party services requested or required in connection with the student's Programme.

blocks.text: Once GSS has paid, committed or become liable to pay such amounts to a third party, any amount which is non-recoverable by GSS will also be non-refundable to the student.
Third-party payments are non-transferable unless the applicable third party permits a transfer.
Where GSS is able to recover all or part of a third-party payment, any amount recovered will be taken into consideration when determining any refund otherwise due to the student.
Refund Policy: Executive Education and CPD Courses
Once payment has been received, cleared and access to the GSS Online Study Portal has been activated for the student, the Course Fee is non-refundable.

Access to the GSS Online Study Portal will ordinarily be activated only after the required payment has been received and cleared. Any exception to this arrangement must be expressly agreed by The Global School of Skills (GSS) (GSS).
Students are therefore advised to carefully review the Course details and ensure that they have selected the correct Course before making payment.
This does not affect any statutory rights which cannot lawfully be excluded or restricted.
Assessments
Assessment for the Special Executive Master Programmes is assignment-based.
Assessment for Professional Certificate and Advanced Professional Certificate Courses is quiz-based and consists of multiple-choice questions.
Students are permitted a maximum of three (3) attempts for each applicable quiz, provided that all required payments have been received and cleared.

Registration

Once GSS has commenced or completed the application and registration service, the Registration Fee is non-refundable, subject to any applicable statutory rights.
Tuition Fees
Following the issuance of a Conditional Offer Letter, the student is required to pay the applicable Tuition Fee in accordance with the payment terms stated by GSS.

Unless otherwise expressly agreed by GSS in writing, all required payments must be received and cleared before the commencement of the Programme in order to confirm the student's place and eligibility to participate.

Where GSS permits payment by instalments, each instalment paid forms part of the Tuition Fee for the Programme and is non-refundable once paid, subject to any statutory rights which cannot lawfully be excluded or restricted.
Students who have not satisfied the applicable payment requirements may not be admitted to, or permitted to continue on, the Programme.
The Tuition Fee covers only those items expressly stated by GSS as being included in the Programme Fee.

Any costs not expressly included in the Programme Fee remain the responsibility of the student. These may include, where applicable, personal expenses, travel, accommodation, visas, immigration requirements, insurance, transportation and other related costs, unless GSS has expressly agreed in writing to provide or cover a specific item.

items: health or medical certificates required for travel;
passports;
visas or transit visas;
travel insurance;
lost or delayed baggage;
missed flights;
missed connecting flights;
refusal of entry at a destination or transit country;
cancelled or delayed flights;
transportation arrangements; or
other matters outside GSS's reasonable control.

blocks.text: Students are strongly encouraged to obtain appropriate travel insurance and ensure that all travel requirements have been satisfied before making non-refundable travel arrangements.
Nothing in this provision excludes liability arising from GSS's own breach of contract or any liability which cannot lawfully be excluded.

Where GSS is able to recover all or part of the amount from the third-party provider, the amount recovered will be taken into consideration.

Where a student is unable to attend the Programme after such arrangements have been made, GSS may permit the student to transfer to another available session, subject to availability, any applicable fare or accommodation difference, and an administrative or change fee.

A student who is unable to attend a Classroom-based Programme or an event may request to be transferred to another available session within GSS's training calendar.
A student may ordinarily reschedule a Programme up to three (3) times at the tuition-fee rate applicable to the original booking, subject to:

items: availability;
any non-recoverable third-party costs;
any difference in travel or accommodation costs; and
the applicable administrative or change fee.

blocks.text: Where a student requests a fourth rescheduling, the student will be required to pay any difference between the original Tuition Fee and the Tuition Fee applicable to the new Programme, together with any applicable administrative, travel or other charges.
Rescheduling is subject to GSS's published training calendar and availability.

Every student is responsible for ensuring that they possess all passports, visas, transit visas, immigration permissions and other documentation required to travel to and attend the Programme.
Where GSS offers a visa-application or visa-support service, GSS's responsibility is limited to providing the specific service expressly agreed with the student.

A visa refusal does not, by itself, create an entitlement to a refund.

Where a student is unable to attend because of a visa refusal, any refund, credit or rescheduling request will be considered in accordance with this Policy, taking into account services already provided and costs or commitments already incurred.
Fees and third-party costs which have already been incurred and are non-recoverable remain non-refundable.

GSS may decline a discretionary refund where the visa refusal resulted from inaccurate or incomplete information supplied by the student, failure to satisfy applicable immigration requirements, late submission of documents, or another matter within the student's reasonable control.

Where cancellation occurs after GSS has incurred costs, made bookings, commenced services or otherwise committed resources specifically in connection with the student's attendance, those amounts may be retained from any refund otherwise payable.

Where cancellation occurs less than four (4) weeks before the Programme commencement date, Tuition Fees will ordinarily be non-refundable where GSS has already committed resources, incurred corresponding costs or cannot reasonably reallocate the student's place.
GSS may, at its discretion, offer a transfer, credit or rescheduling option instead of a refund.

Where GSS cancels a Programme and is unable to deliver it or provide a reasonably equivalent rescheduled session, students will be entitled to an appropriate refund of fees paid for services which GSS will not provide.
Where a Programme is rescheduled, students may elect to attend the rescheduled Programme subject to the applicable terms.
Nothing in this section limits any statutory remedy available to the student.

items: Top-Up Degree tuition fees are determined by the applicable University and may be subject to change;
final certificates and awards are issued by the awarding University;

This does not affect your statutory rights.

Once payment has been received in full, cleared into the GSS bank account and credited to the relevant Corporate or Business Account Wallet, the Wallet funds are non-refundable except where otherwise agreed in writing or required by law.

Unused funds remaining in the Corporate or Business Account Wallet may continue to be allocated to eligible Programmes or Courses available on the GSS Online Study Portal.
Nothing in this section excludes any right or remedy which cannot lawfully be excluded.

Nothing in this Policy affects your statutory rights.

Where a student does not otherwise have a contractual or statutory right to a refund, GSS may, at its sole discretion, consider a request for:

items: a partial refund;
Programme credit;
deferral;
transfer to another Programme; or
rescheduling.

blocks.text: Examples may include serious illness, bereavement or other substantial circumstances outside the student's reasonable control.

Approval under this section is discretionary and will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Previous decisions do not create an entitlement or precedent for future applications.

Any refund or cancellation will be considered in accordance with:

items: this Refund and Cancellation Policy;
the student's Study Contract;
the applicable Offer Letter;
any Programme-specific terms;
the terms of any relevant third-party provider; and
applicable law.

items: INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: It is the School’s policy to conduct its business in an honest and ethical manner. The School takes a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption and is committed to acting professionally, fairly and with integrity in all of its business dealings and relationships wherever the School operates.
The School will uphold all laws relevant to countering bribery and corruption including the Bribery Act 2010 (‘the Act’), in respect of its conduct both at home and abroad.
The purpose of this policy is:
(a) To set out the responsibilities of the School, and of those working for it, in observing and upholding our position on bribery and corruption; and
(b) To provide information and guidance to those working for the School on how to recognize and deal with bribery and corruption issues.

Bribery and corruption are punishable for individuals by up to ten years' imprisonment and if the School is found to have taken part in corruption it could face an unlimited fine, be excluded from tendering for public contracts and face damage to its reputation. The School therefore takes its legal responsibilities very seriously.

In this policy, third party means any individual or organization you come into contact with during the course of your work for the School, and includes students, external funders, customers, suppliers, distributors, business contacts, agents, advisers, and government and public bodies, including their advisors, representatives and officials, politicians and political parties.
References in this policy to obtaining written approval includes obtaining approval by e-mail.

items: WHO IS COVERED BY THE POLICY?

blocks.text: This policy applies to all individuals working at all levels and grades, and includes all employees (whether permanent, fixed-term or temporary), honorary staff, consultants, contractors, trainees, seconded staff, homeworkers, casual workers and agency staff, volunteers, interns, agents, sponsors, or any other person associated with us, or any of our subsidiaries or their employees, wherever located (collectively referred to as workers in this policy), The Act applies to conduct both within and outside the UK.

items: WHAT IS BRIBERY?

blocks.text: A bribe is an inducement or reward offered, promised or provided in order to gain any commercial, contractual, regulatory or personal advantage. At the end of this document there is a schedule setting out some scenarios that illustrate potential bribery.

items: GIFTS AND HOSPITALITY

blocks.text: In addition to the requirements set out below, you must register any gifts or hospitality given or received with an estimated value in excess of £100 with either your Faculty Manager or Divisional Head. The details of how to do this are set out in Paragraph 9.2 below. Further, you must obtain the written approval (which includes by e-mail) of your line manager in relation to any gifts or hospitality given or received with an estimated monetary value in excess of £500 (see paragraph 9.2 below). You may register or obtain consent on a voluntary basis in relation to gifts or hospitality below the relevant figures. Paragraph 4.5 also contains a registration requirement.

The School recognises that the practice of the giving and receiving of business gifts or hospitality varies between countries and regions and what may be normal and acceptable in one region may not be in another. The test to be applied is whether in all the circumstances the gift or hospitality is reasonable and justifiable. The intention behind the gift or hospitality should always be considered.
Hospitality

This policy does not prohibit normal and appropriate hospitality (given and received) to or from third parties, for the purposes of establishing or maintaining good business relationships or improving or maintaining our reputation or image.
Gifts
The giving or receipt of gifts is not prohibited, if the following requirements are met:

(a) it is not made with the intention of influencing a third party to obtain or retain business or a business advantage, or to reward the provision or retention of business or a business advantage, or in explicit or implicit exchange for favours or benefits;
(b) it is given in the School’s name, not in your name;
(c) it does not include cash or a cash equivalent (such as gift certificates or vouchers);
(d) it is appropriate in the circumstances. For example, in the UK it is customary for small gifts to be given at Christmas time;
(e) taking into account the reason for the gift, it is of an appropriate type and value and given at an appropriate time; and
(f) it is given openly, not secretly.

Gifts should not be offered to, or accepted from, government officials or representatives, or politicians or political parties, without the prior approval of your manager. Any such gifts must be registered regardless of value.

items: WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE?

blocks.text: It is not acceptable for you (or someone on your behalf) to:

(a) give, promise to give, or offer, a payment, gift or hospitality with the expectation or hope that either a personal or business advantage will be received, or to reward either a personal or business advantage already given;
(b) give, promise to give, or offer, a payment, gift or hospitality to a government official, agent or representative to "facilitate" or expedite a routine procedure;
(c) accept payment from a third party that you know or suspect is offered with the expectation that it will obtain either a personal or business advantage for them;

(d) accept a gift or hospitality from a third party if you know or suspect that it is offered or provided with an expectation that either a personal or business advantage will be provided by the School in return;

(e) accept a gift or hospitality from a third party who is tendering for a contract to be awarded by the School either on its own or jointly with other parties and for a period of three months after the award of the contract;
(f) turn a blind eye to any of the above;
(g) threaten or retaliate against another worker who has refused to commit a bribery offence or who has raised concerns under this policy; or
(h) engage in any activity that might lead to a breach of this policy.

items: FACILITATION PAYMENTS AND KICKBACKS

blocks.text: The School does not make, and will not accept, facilitation payments or "kickbacks" of any kind. Facilitation payments are typically small, unofficial payments made to secure or expedite a routine government action by a government official. They are not commonly paid in the UK, but are common in some other jurisdictions.

If you are asked to make a payment on the School’s behalf, you should always be mindful of what the payment is for and whether the amount requested is proportionate to the goods or services provided. You should always ask for a receipt which details the reason for the payment. If you have any suspicions, concerns or queries regarding a payment, you should raise these with the Secretary’s Office.
All workers must avoid any activity that might lead to, or suggest, that a facilitation payment or kickback will be made or accepted by the School.

items: DONATIONS

blocks.text: We do not make any contributions to political parties.

items: YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

blocks.text: You must ensure that you read, understand and comply with this policy.

The prevention, detection and reporting of bribery and other forms of corruption are the responsibility of all those working for the School or under its control. All workers are required to avoid any activity that might lead to, or suggest, a breach of this policy.

You must notify either the Secretary’s Office or follow the steps set out in the Whistleblowing Policy as soon as possible if you believe or suspect that a conflict with this policy has occurred, or may occur in the future. If you are unsure whether a particular act constitutes bribery or corruption, please contact the Secretary’s Office.

Any employee who breaches this policy will face disciplinary action, which could result in dismissal for gross misconduct. We reserve our right to terminate our contractual relationship with other workers if they breach this policy.

items: RECORD-KEEPING

blocks.text: The School must keep financial records and have appropriate internal controls in place which will evidence the business reason for making payments to third parties.

If you are required to register a gift or hospitality under this policy you must complete the Gifts and Hospitality Registration form and send it to either your Faculty Manager or Divisional Head who will maintain a Register of Gifts and Hospitality (which can consist of storing the forms electronically). You must register any gift or hospitality within 28 days. Requests to your line manager for written approval (which includes by e-mail) of gifts or hospitality must be submitted in advance where possible to allow time for a decision to be made.

You must ensure that all claims relating to hospitality and gifts and other payments to third parties are submitted in accordance with the relevant School policy and specifically record the reason for the expenditure.

All accounts, invoices, memoranda and other documents and records relating to dealings with third parties, such as clients, suppliers and business contacts, should be prepared and maintained with strict accuracy and completeness. No accounts must be kept "off-book" to facilitate or conceal improper payments.

items: RISK ASSESSMENT AND KNOWING WHO YOU ARE DEALING WITH

blocks.text: The Secretary’s Office will review annually the corruption and bribery risk that the School faces.

It is also the responsibility of all workers to bring to the attention of the Secretary’s Office any potential new risk which may arise when it arises, rather than waiting to report it in the annual risk assessment.
All workers must understand who they doing business with and guidance on this issue can be obtained from the Secretary’s Office. This process is known as due diligence.

items: WHAT TO DO IF YOU BECOME INVOLVED IN BRIBERY OR CORRUPTION

blocks.text: It is important that you inform your Head of Department as soon as possible even if you suspect that it may happen in the future.

items: PROTECTION

blocks.text: Workers who refuse to accept or offer a bribe, or those who raise concerns or report another's wrongdoing, are sometimes worried about possible repercussions. The School aims to encourage openness and will support anyone who raises genuine concerns in good faith under this policy, even if they turn out to be mistaken.

The School is committed to ensuring no one suffers any detrimental treatment as a result of refusing to take part in bribery or corruption, or because of reporting in good faith their suspicion that an actual or potential bribery or other corruption offence has taken place, or may take place in the future. Detrimental treatment includes dismissal, disciplinary action, threats or other unfavourable treatment connected with raising a concern. If you believe that you have suffered any such treatment, you should inform your Head of Department immediately.

items: POLICY COMMUNICATION

blocks.text: Our zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption should be communicated to all suppliers, contractors and business partners. A standard Anti-Corruption and Bribery clause, which is available on the Anti-Corruption and Bribery web pages should be inserted into all contracts where possible and where not, the contract should contain a clause that provides the School with the same level of protection as afforded by the standard clause unless otherwise advised by the Secretary’s Office.

items: WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE POLICY?

blocks.text: The School Council has overall responsibility for ensuring that this policy complies with our legal and ethical obligations, and that all those under the School’s control comply with it.
The Secretary’s Office has primary and day-to-day responsibility for implementing this policy, for monitoring its use and effectiveness and dealing with any queries on its interpretation.

items: MONITORING AND REVIEW

blocks.text: The Heads of Departments will monitor the effectiveness and review the implementation of this policy, regularly considering its suitability, adequacy and effectiveness. Any improvements identified will be made as soon as possible. All workers are responsible for the success of this policy and should ensure they use it to disclose any suspected danger or wrongdoing.
Workers are invited to comment on this policy and suggest ways in which it might be improved. Comments, suggestions and queries should be addressed to the Secretary’s Office.

This policy does not form part of any employee's contract of employment and it may be amended at any time. You will be notified of any changes to this policy by the placing of updated versions of it on the School’s website so please refer to the website for the most up to date version.

The following is a list of possible scenarios that may arise during the course of your working for the School and which may raise concerns under anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws. The list is not exhaustive and is for illustration only.
If you encounter any of these situations while working for the School, you must report them promptly to your Head of Department OR using the procedure set out in the Whistleblowing Policy:

(c) a third party insists on receiving a commission or fee payment before committing to sign up to a contract with us, or carrying out a government function or process for us;
(d) a third party asks for payment in cash and/or refuses to sign a formal commission or fee agreement, or to provide an invoice or receipt for a payment made;
(e) a third party asks that payment be made to a country or geographic location different from where the third party resides or conducts business;
(f) a third party asks for an unexpected additional fee or commission to "facilitate" a service;
(g) a third party demands lavish entertainment or gifts before commencing or continuing contractual negotiations or provision of services;
(h) a third party asks that a payment is made to "overlook" potential legal violations;
(i) a third party asks that you provide employment or some other advantage to a friend or relative;
(j) you receive an invoice from a third party that appears to be non-standard or customized;
(k) a third party insists on the use of side letters or refuses to put agreed terms in writing;
(l) you notice that we have been invoiced for a commission or fee payment that appears large given the service stated to have been provided;
(m) a third party requests or requires the use of an agent, intermediary, consultant, distributor or supplier that is not typically used by or known to us;
(n) you are offered an unusually generous gift or offered lavish hospitality by a third party.

This Agreement, hereinafter referred to as the "Partnership Agreement," establishes the terms and conditions governing the collaborative partnership between the The Global School of Skills (GSS) UK ("GSS"), a globally recognized EdTech Institution with a presence in London, Islamabad, Lagos, and Dubai, and the Charities they work with (collectively referred to as the "Parties").

The purpose of this Partnership Agreement is to outline the framework and responsibilities of the Parties in achieving common objectives related to education, fundraising, and the advancement of educational opportunities. This Agreement encompasses a multifaceted partnership aimed at raising funds to support educational initiatives, fostering access to quality education, and facilitating the pursuit of degrees through GSS's affiliated universities.

Both GSS and the Charities recognize the transformative power of education as a force for societal progress and individual empowerment. This partnership seeks to harness their respective expertise and resources to bridge educational gaps, particularly in underserved regions, and promote inclusivity in education. By combining their strengths, the Parties aim to make education accessible, affordable, and enriching for a broader spectrum of individuals, thereby contributing to the overall development of communities and societies.

This Agreement sets forth the rights, obligations, and operational guidelines governing the partnership between GSS and these Charities, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and the shared commitment to the mission of providing educational opportunities to those who might otherwise face barriers to learning. The Parties understand the significance of their collaboration in advancing the cause of education and hereby pledge to work diligently and in good faith to achieve their mutually beneficial goals.

By entering into this Partnership Agreement, both GSS and the Charities intend to create a lasting impact on education, empower learners, and inspire positive change, reflecting their shared vision of a world where educational opportunities are within reach for all.

The Parties, in recognition of their shared commitment to the transformative power of education and their desire to make a substantial impact on the educational landscape, hereby enter into this Partnership Agreement with the following objectives:

2.1.1. Fundraising Initiatives: The Parties commit to a collaborative effort to organize and execute fundraising initiatives, campaigns, and activities with the primary goal of mobilizing financial resources. These resources are intended to be allocated to support a wide range of educational initiatives, programs, and projects, with a special emphasis on reaching and empowering underserved individuals who may face obstacles in accessing quality education.
2.1.2. Fund Utilization: The funds raised through the joint fundraising efforts shall be allocated strategically to:

items: Educate deserving learners, including but not limited to beneficiaries of these Charities on the GSS Platform as well as GSS's affiliate Universities' Platform.
Enhance educational infrastructure, resources, and materials that contribute to the overall quality and accessibility of their education.

Foster the development and expansion of educational programs, initiatives, and projects aimed at addressing educational disparities and promoting learning opportunities for individuals across various socioeconomic backgrounds.

blocks.text: 2.1.3. Sustainable Funding: The Parties aspire to establish a sustainable source of funding for ongoing and future educational initiatives, ensuring that the impact of this partnership extends well into the future.

2.2.1. Educational Opportunities: GSS shall facilitate and promote educational opportunities, including but not limited to degree programs, certifications, and skill development courses, offered through its affiliated universities.

2.2.2. Accessible Learning: The Parties commit to making education accessible and affordable to a broader spectrum of learners, including those who may not have had the opportunity to pursue higher education without financial support.

2.2.3. Academic Support: GSS, in collaboration with the Charities, shall provide academic support, mentorship, and guidance to beneficiaries pursuing educational programs, fostering an environment conducive to academic excellence.

2.2.4. Monitoring and Evaluation: The Parties acknowledge the importance of ongoing assessment and improvement of educational initiatives. Therefore, they will jointly conduct periodic evaluations of program outcomes and impact to ensure that resources are utilized effectively and that learners receive high-quality education.

The Parties recognize that education serves as a catalyst for individual empowerment, community development, and societal progress. As such, they are united in their commitment to advancing education as a means of fostering personal growth, economic opportunity, and positive societal transformation.

By working together under this Partnership Agreement, the Parties aspire to unlock the full potential of education and create lasting change in the lives of beneficiaries, their communities, and society as a whole.

3.1.1. Collaborative Efforts: GSS and Charity shall actively collaborate to conceive, plan, and execute various fundraising initiatives, campaigns, and activities. These efforts are undertaken with the overarching objective of generating substantial financial resources to support educational programs, initiatives, and projects.

3.1.2 Diverse Fundraising Approaches: The Parties shall explore and employ diverse fundraising approaches, leveraging their respective networks, resources, and creativity to maximize the impact of these initiatives. Fundraising may encompass online and offline events, donor outreach, grant applications, and partnerships with other organizations that share the mission of advancing education.

3.1.3 Beneficiary-Centric Fundraising: Fundraising initiatives shall prioritize the needs and aspirations of the beneficiaries, aiming to ensure that financial support is allocated strategically to empower underserved individuals and communities through education.

3.1.4 GSS Sponsorship Rights: In recognition of GSS's sole sponsorship of these initiatives, GSS reserves exclusive rights to approve all fundraising activities, campaigns, and events. This includes, but is not limited to, the selection of partners, event formats, fundraising channels, and promotional materials. GSS's prior written consent is required for any deviations from agreed plans or for introducing new fundraising initiatives.

3.2.2. Oversight and Control: Given GSS's role as the sole sponsor, GSS shall assume primary oversight and control over the management of the Dedicated Business Account. This includes but is not limited to monitoring inflows and outflows, maintaining accurate financial records, and ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations governing charitable donations.

3.2.3. Auditing and Reporting: Independent auditors appointed by GSS shall conduct regular audits of the Dedicated Business Account to ensure financial transactions' accuracy, transparency, and accountability. As appropriate, audit reports shall be shared with GSS, Charity, and other stakeholders.

3.3.1. This ensures that financial constraints do not hinder their pursuit of education.

3.3.2. Responsible Allocation: The Parties commit to responsible financial allocation, with GSS overseeing and approving fund disbursements to ensure efficient, effective utilization aligned with educational objectives and donor intent.

4.1.2. Utilization of Donations: Donations received through fundraising initiatives shall be exclusively allocated to the following educational purposes:

items: Tuition fees and related educational expenses, facilitating the education of beneficiaries on the GSS platform.
